Hi Aaron / Sonal —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As promised, I put together a short "sprint grid" to align costs vs performance controls we'll iterate during the onboarding window (batching, KV caching, quant profiles, routing fallbacks). Attached: a draft MOP (acero_mop_v1.pdf) and a starter KV/quant matrix (kv_profile_matrix.xlsx).

Quick asks from our side so we can finalize the grid before the sync:
- Can you confirm expected steady-state QPS and peak QPS (per region)?
- Typical average and 95th-percentile prompt token lengths (sample traffic shape helps us pick batch targets).
- Any hard latency SLOs (p50/p95) that we should treat as blockers?

Proposed 30-minute sync today at 11:00 PDT to walk the grid and assign owners. If that works, I’ll send an invite and a short agenda: 1) baseline metrics, 2) initial quant/profile recommendations, 3) canary rollout plan, 4) ops checkpoints.

Attachments: acero_mop_v1.pdf (draft), kv_profile_matrix.xlsx (starter).

Thanks,

Thanks — attaching a short traffic snapshot (qps_and_prompts.csv) that shows our expected steady (120 qps) and short peaks (~600 qps for 10–15m windows). Average prompt length: ~180 tokens; 95th: ~620 tokens. Latency target: p95 <= 850ms in US west.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-25T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch readiness: cost-performance sprint grid for Acero Health

Aaron / team —

Thanks for the snapshot — that helps a lot. A few pragmatic notes ahead of the call so we can keep the sync tactical:

1) Quantization profile recommendation (first pass):
   - Canary: q4_0 (FP4-style) on 10% traffic for quality validation.
   - Bulk: int8-dynamic only if canary metrics (perplexity + user-facing regression tests) pass.

2) Batching targets:
   - For average prompt (~180 tokens) target batching size ~8–12 to preserve p50 while reducing tokens/unit cost.
   - For peaky windows, use adaptive batching with a hard cap at 24 to avoid p95 blowouts.

3) KV caching and prefetch:
   - Expect 60–75% cache hit for short-session flows; set prefetch threshold for sequences >200 tokens.

4) Routing policy / graceful degradation:
   - Primary: west-us low-latency pool (single-AZ).
   - Fallback: cheaper mid-tier pool (cheaper quant) in same region with automatic 5s window to avoid amplify latencies.

5) Canary & rollout: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with automated quality checks at each step (latency + a small eval prompt set).

Action items before the call:
- Monica: confirm SLOs (p50/p95) and list of eval prompts we should run against canary.
- Aaron: share sample production traces (headers + timing) and any DO NOT TOUCH policies.
- Priyom: prepare a short runbook for KV prefetch thresholds we’ll propose.

I’ll cover cost tradeoffs on the call and Marissa will own the rollout plan and MOP updates.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aaron Patel <aaron@acerohealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-25T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch readiness: cost-performance sprint grid for Acero Health — technical notes

Quick technical notes based on Aaron's traffic snapshot and Vivek's recommendations:

- Batching: for 180-token average prompts, batching window of 6–10ms yields effective batch sizes in the 8–12 range under steady load. We'll start with a conservative 8 and ramp if p95 stable.
- KV cache: set TTL for session-level caches to 7 minutes by default; prefetch when sequence length >200 tokens or when user session has >2 prior requests in 60s. Expect warm-hit ratio ~65%.
- Quant profiles: see attachment (kv_profile_matrix.xlsx) — contains test vector performance numbers from our internal bench for q4_0 and int8-dynamic across sequence lengths 128/256/512/1024.
- Observability hooks: we will enable token-level cost exposure and per-model latency breakdowns for the canary so you can see unit economics in near-real time.

I attached the kv_profile_matrix.xlsx (starter). I’ll bring a short demo of the canary dashboard to the sync.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
